info.name: Doodle Meeting Scheduler API
info.description:
Full scenario-coverage collection for the Doodle-style meeting scheduler backend
(Spring Boot, `com.doodle.challenge`) - Users, Time Slots, Meetings, Participants,
and Availability.

**How to run**
- Run the whole collection top-to-bottom with the Collection Runner (folders 01-07
  are ordered as one continuous story: register users, build a calendar, schedule a
  meeting, exercise participants/availability against it, then cancel it last).
- Individual requests can also be run standalone once the chain has executed at
  least once in the session, since IDs/timestamps are cached as collection variables.
- Re-running the whole collection from scratch is safe: emails are randomized per run
  (`{{$randomUUID}}`), so user registration never collides with a previous run.

**Auth**: every endpoint requires `Authorization: Basic base64(email:password)`
except `POST /users`, Swagger/OpenAPI docs, and the health/metrics actuator endpoints
(see `SecurityConfig`). Each request in this collection sets its own Basic Auth using
whichever persona (owner / participant / outsider) the scenario calls for.

**Errors**: all error responses are RFC 7807 `ProblemDetail` bodies
(`type`, `title`, `status`, `detail`) - see `GlobalExceptionHandler`.

**Base URL**: defaults to `http://localhost:8080` (plain `mvn spring-boot:run` /
local run). If you're using the bundled `docker-compose.yml` instead, the app is
published on the host as `http://localhost:8088` - update the `baseUrl` variable
(or the imported environment) accordingly.

exec: // Seed reusable future timestamps once per Runner session, so every
// on the same slot boundaries without recomputing them mid-run.

item.name: 01 - Users

request.description: Registers the user who will own every Meeting/TimeSlot created later in this collection. Registration is on the security permit-list, so no credentials are sent.
A second user who will be invited to the owner's meeting.
A third user with no relationship to the meeting - used to exercise 403 Forbidden scenarios (non-owner mutation, responding on someone else's behalf).
Blank name, malformed email, and a password under the 8-character minimum should all be rejected by bean validation in one shot.
Re-registering the owner's email should be rejected - exact status depends on how the unique constraint violation is mapped (a 500 here would indicate a missing exception handler worth flagging).

exec: pm.test("Returns the owner's own profile", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().id).to.eql(pm.collectionVariables.get("ownerId")); });

request.description: Every endpoint except POST /users, Swagger, and health/metrics requires Basic auth. This request deliberately omits credentials.

item.description: User registration and lookup. Also covers the Basic Auth permit-list (registration is open, everything else requires credentials) and validation/uniqueness edge cases.

item.name: 02 - Time Slots
Create Time Slot - Primary (for the Meeting later)

request.description: This slot is converted into a Meeting in folder 03, which is what drives the "slot not free" / "slot backs an active meeting" conflict scenarios later.
Same owner, exact same range as the slot just created - SlotOverlapValidator must reject this.

item.name: Create Time Slot - Partial Overlap (409 Conflict)

request.description: Starts 15 minutes into slot 1 and extends past it - overlap detection must catch partial overlaps, not just identical ranges.
Missing startTime and endTime - both are @NotNull.

item.name: Create Time Slot - Invalid Range, Start After End (422)

request.description: startTime/endTime are both present (passes bean validation) but reversed, so TimeRange.of throws InvalidTimeRangeException -> 422, distinct from the 400s above.

item.name: Create Time Slot - User Not Found (404)
Create Time Slot - Second (for reschedule/status/delete demo)

exec: pm.test("Both slots created so far are present", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().totalElements).to.be.at.least(2); });

item.name: List Time Slots - Page Size Capped at 100

request.description: Requesting an oversized page size should be silently capped to MAX_PAGE_SIZE (100), not rejected or honored as-is.

exec: pm.test("Page size is capped, not honored verbatim", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().size).to.equal(100); });

item.name: Update Time Slot - Reschedule FREE Slot (200)
Change Time Slot Status - Validation Error (400)

request.description: status is @NotNull - an empty body must fail validation before reaching the service.

item.name: Change Time Slot Status - Mark BUSY (200)

request.description: Manually toggling status BUSY without a backing meeting - this is what the next request uses to prove delete is rejected purely on status, independent of whether a Meeting actually references the slot.

item.name: Delete Time Slot - Conflict, Slot is BUSY (409)
Change Time Slot Status - Mark FREE Again (200)
Delete Time Slot - Already Deleted, Not Found (404)

request.description: Soft-deleted slots are treated as not-found on subsequent access.

item.description: CRUD over a user's calendar slots: creation with overlap detection, pagination, rescheduling, manual FREE/BUSY toggling, and deletion rules. Uses a second, disposable slot (freeSlotId) so the primary slot (timeSlotId) stays available for the Meeting scenarios in folder 03.

item.name: 03 - Meetings
Schedule Meeting (converts timeSlotId, no initial invitees)

request.description: Converts the FREE slot from folder 02 into a Meeting. This marks the slot BUSY, which the next few requests rely on to demonstrate conflict handling.

item.name: Schedule Meeting - Slot Not Free (409 Conflict)
Schedule Meeting - Time Slot Not Found (404)
Schedule Meeting - Validation Error, Missing Fields (400)

request.description: Creates a throwaway FREE slot, then the next request tries to schedule a meeting on it inviting a non-existent user - the whole operation should roll back (404, not a partially-created meeting).

item.name: Schedule Meeting - Invitee Not Found, Follow-up (404)
Update Time Slot - Conflict, Slot Not Free (409)

request.description: Rescheduling is only allowed on a FREE slot; timeSlotId is BUSY (backing the meeting scheduled above).

item.name: Delete Time Slot - Conflict, Backs an Active Meeting (409)
Update Meeting - Forbidden, Not the Owner (403)

request.description: MeetingPolicy restricts update/cancel/participant-management to the owner only.

item.name: Update Meeting - Validation Error, Blank Title (400)

item.description: Scheduling (FREE slot -> Meeting conversion), lookup, owner-only updates, and the resulting knock-on conflicts on the underlying time slot (not-free, backs-a-meeting). Cancellation lives in folder 06, after Availability and Participants, so the meeting stays active long enough for those scenarios to use it.

item.name: 04 - Participants

request.description: The same user cannot be invited twice.

item.name: Invite Participant - Forbidden, Not the Owner (403)

request.description: Only the meeting owner may invite - a fellow participant cannot invite others.

item.name: Invite Participant - Validation Error, Missing userId (400)
Remove Participant - Forbidden, Not the Owner (403)

request.description: Removal is owner-only, same as inviting.

item.name: Respond to Invitation - Forbidden, Wrong User (403)

request.description: Responding to an invitation is not owner-gated, but IS restricted to the invited user themselves - the outsider cannot accept on the participant's behalf.

item.name: Respond to Invitation - Validation Error, Invalid Status (400)

request.description: INVITED is a structurally valid enum value but not a valid response - the service (not bean validation) rejects anything other than ACCEPTED/DECLINED.

item.description: Invite / respond / remove lifecycle on the meeting created in folder 03. Covers owner-only enforcement, self-only response enforcement, duplicate-invite conflicts, and the not-a-real-status validation branch.

item.name: 05 - Availability
Get Availability - Full Window, No Status Filter (200)

request.description: timeSlotId is BUSY (backing the active meeting) and scratchSlotId is FREE - both should fall in this window.

exec: pm.test("busySlots is empty when filtering to FREE", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().busySlots).to.have.lengthOf(0); });
pm.test("freeSlots is empty when filtering to BUSY", function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().freeSlots).to.have.lengthOf(0); });

item.name: Get Availability - Invalid Range, From After To (422)

request.description: from/to are swapped, so TimeRange.of rejects the window the same way it rejects a slot with start after end.

item.name: Get Availability - Missing Required Query Params (400)

request.description: from and to have no defaults - omitting them should fail request binding, not NPE.

item.description: The aggregated free/busy view for a user over a window, run while the meeting from folder 03 is still active so BUSY has a real slot to show.

item.name: 06 - Meeting Cancellation
Cancel Meeting - Forbidden, Not the Owner (403)
Get Meeting - Not Found After Cancel (404)

request.description: Cancelling hard-deletes the Meeting row (see MeetingService.cancelMeeting), so it should be gone entirely, not just marked cancelled.

item.name: Cancel Meeting - Not Found, Already Cancelled (404)
Verify Time Slot is FREE Again (200)
Delete Time Slot (204) - now that no meeting backs it

item.description: Owner-only cancellation, run last since it hard-deletes the meeting and frees its time slot - everything in folders 03-05 depends on that meeting still existing.

item.name: 07 - Auth & Authorization

request.description: On the security permit-list alongside /actuator/health/**, /actuator/prometheus, Swagger UI, and /v3/api-docs/**.

item.name: Protected Endpoint With Malformed Basic Header (401)

request.description: Sends a syntactically-broken Authorization header (invalid base64) rather than omitting it entirely.

item.description: Endpoints on the SecurityConfig permit-list vs. everything else, plus malformed-credential handling.
